newsitem.title: GREECE: GREEK DEPOS, BONDS IDLE, DRACHMA UPTICKS VS ECU.
newsitem.headline: GREEK DEPOS, BONDS IDLE, DRACHMA UPTICKS VS ECU.

text.p: The drachma was ranging against
the ecu, firming 10 ticks to 308.50 in late Monday dealings on
the back of the central bank's selling of 60 million ecus for
drachmas at the fixing, dealers said.
Depos, forex forwards and bonds were little changed, holding
mid-session levels, dealers said.
"The central bank's move to sell 60 million ecus for
drachmas at the fixing showed its determination to honour its
commitment to the hard drachma policy," said a forex dealer at a
foreign bank.
Ecu/drachma spent most of the session in the 308.45/60
corridor after opening at 308.40/50.
"Ecu/drachma is hovering around 308.50 in late trade, off an
intraday high of 308.85," he said.
Fixed coupon bonds and FRNs were fluctuating narrowly,
holding mid-session price levels in late trading unaffected by
the finance ministry's announcement pertaining to the amount of
the FRN auction on August 21 and fresh cuts in T-bill rates,
dealers said.
The finance ministry will seek to raise 100 billion drachmas
via its FRN auction.
"The amount was expected and the market did not react to the
news," said a foreign bank dealer. "The key is liquidity and it
looks if the system will get some help from regular, end-month
inflows from pension funds."
The treasury will also slash three-, six- and 12-month
T-bill rates by 10 basis points to 8.4 percent, 8.7 percent and
9.5 percent from August 19. It will also offer 12-month T-bills
to the public on August 20.
The 10-year bond was trading around 94.50 in late dealings,
sustaining its 402 basis point spread over Bunds, dealers said.
